title: Picnic on the Lawn
subtitle: Ham, bread and drink ... I assume they taste much better than critters.

content.text: The story has come to a new stage.
It is fascinating. It has plots of unwavering loyalty, survival from the jaws of death, and even a little bit of ... unconventional excitement!
Raise your head, and you will see this splendid spotlight grilling the top of our heads like a stove heating a frying pan.
We mumble, and mumble, and mumble ... something like arcanists, new changes, perseverance, and the "Storm." Right, that's it! The "Storm"!
The "Storm" is no longer something new here. Everyone in the story talks about the "Storm." People don't find it attractive anymore.
Once you turn the camera out of the spotlight, you'll see many other people on the stage. Many, many other f*****g people.
Who are they?

branch.text: The other actors. Actors who are different from you.
Their name won't be listed in the cast at the end of the movie. Not even a poor "St. Pavlov Squad Leader A."

content.text: Where do they come from?

branch.text: Neat question. People always need a place to come from.
Then I will give you a neat answer as well, you inquisitive little thing. They came from their mothers' tummies. Can you understand it? Is it too difficult for you?

content.text: They're a bunch of people, a bunch of people just like you, though there are still differences between you and them. Open their bellies, and you can find everything that should be there—the liver, the stomach, the spleen, the lungs, and the heart.
Their faces are clear to be seen. Look at them carefully, carefully. Oh, you might have met one or two of them.
They come from the same institution as yours, the St. Pavlov Foundation.
Eve from the France branch, La from the Egypt branch, and the Matryoshka from the Russia branch.

Oh right, your first friend made in a branch, that—that young man with a red nose—Ken! Ken from the Scotland branch. You looked here, you looked there, you couldn't find him anywhere, however hard you tried.
Where did he go?

branch.text: Good question. I'll help you find him.

content.text: Let's keep looking around, but this time, vertically instead of horizontally. That's right! Upside vertical. Don't be afraid of that radiant spotlight, look there! Ignore the risk of blinding your eyes!
And you see it. A white umbrella, bigger and wider than any umbrella you have seen. Those green flashes stinging your eyes is the price you have to pay for finding it.
The white umbrella is a shelter from the rain, saving that Orange-hair girl in white for you.
And you have witnessed how people standing in the pouring "Storm" without shelter fade away.
Like your little friends, and Ken from the Scotland branch.
Remember the differences I just mentioned?

branch.text: A great time to keep silent.
Your ugly trauma, a mixture of your mental issues and miserable past, would burst out in the next second, making everyone's heart twitch.

content.text: But think otherwise.
If the truth were known to all—today's not real, and there's no tomorrow, I'm going to eat my shoes, and an asteroid is falling—then all of them would go crazy.
Those "pigeons" valuing sense above anything won't sit aside and let this happen.
So they made the most sensible choice. The huge white umbrella has only sheltered those qualified people. "Qualified" according to their standard.
Now, let's cross our arms and make an arrogant judgment like those cynics, "How cruel it is!" And then, you may start contemplating.
Should they all go aboard the ark? Can this ark carry these many people?
Try to raise the question as peacefully and slowly as you can. And their enthusiasm will be dampened and let out a sound like what you hear when you pour water into a heated pan—sssss ...
... What about their feelings?

branch.text: Their feelings. Oh, they! You mean Eve, La, and the Matryoshka! Of course, you care about your friends. That's a virtue of yours I won't forget.

content.text: In order to understand their feelings, you need to bend down and reach. That's right, reach for the dark corner under the stage.
Until your fingertip is wrapped by soft, warm, and considerate black velvet, as comfortable as a mother's singing to her baby in a crib.
That's what the people without a shelter above them are feeling now.

branch.text: More silence. You are really good at finding the right timing for your silence, just like my friend and I are experts in farting soundlessly in the elevator cart.

content.text: My hypocrite and dumb friend, think about it in a different way.
Who knows how much garbage there is under the stage? There may be liquid seeping out of rotten pastry and dairy products, intrusions of American cockroach with sleek abdomen crawling everywhere ...
Who can say it's not a blessing to know nothing about the truth?
Especially when you can't leave this shitty place.

items.text: Picnic on the Lawn

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Roast leg of lamb ... Wellington steak ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Turkish kebab ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah ... I want meat ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hmm? Are you hungry?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Worry not, worry not. The leaves of the potatoes we planted have turned yellow!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Ms. Druvis said this is the harvest time! Let's dig them out and make shepherd's pie!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Potato? Vegetable? ... No. I don't want them anymore.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I've been eating healthy salads for a month!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I want meat ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I want rich, juicy, meaty, sinewy, savory, sizzling meat!!
Regulus suddenly springs to her feet.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wait! ... It smells so good. That's meat!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Where's that smell coming from?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hmm ... I do smell something good as well ...
Sotheby stands on tiptoe, seeking the source of the incredible smell.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I'll take a look!
Regulus rubs her stomach, grabs her bag, and dashes out.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Wait, Regulus! The critters' lair is over there!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Critters?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Haha, no worries! Critter is a type of meat! Roast it over fire and a square meal is here!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah, it smells so good ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: It's over here ...
She has gone.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh no, what can I do ...

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Father said some critters could cause hallucination and diarrhea if eaten ...!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: What's going on, Ms. Sotheby? Why are you here walking around alone?
APPLe floats in the air and looks around them.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Em, where is Captain?

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Oh, good to see you here!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Regulus said she smelled meat ... and went straight to the forest to catch critters!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: ... Waffle!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: It has been too long since we last had Dr. Papper. Does Captain finally start to have a senior moment?

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Let's hurry over and take a look.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: The smell of food is unusual. It's verdant over there. There may well be other dangers lurking somewhere.
Regulus's figure appears among the trees.
The aroma of food has also become more intense.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: This is weird. Where on earth does the smell come from?
Regulus is also looking for the answer to the same question.
She looks down, scrabbling in the weeds. As she goes through them, the weeds unexpectedly shake, out of which springs up a black shadow.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Whoa!

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Blimey, it's a Carbuncle! Regulus, it's not edible!
There comes another one.
One after another, until Regulus has an armful of angry Carbuncles.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: That's the lair of Carbuncles. They've been stirred up!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Whoa ... a bumper harvest of critters ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Come and help!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Hold on, Captain! We're coming!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oooh ... Are they really all inedible?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: I did smell the sizzling meat ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: It's somewhere around here, right around ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh, hi.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Whoaaaa—!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Who are you?!
An athletic figure shows up from behind the bushes.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Lilya?

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: What are you doing here ...
Lilya throws her bag at their feet ...
A roasted leg of lamb, wrapped in tinfoil, falls out of her bag.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I got you something good.
Roasted pork knuckle, farmers sausage, black forest ham, some unknown drinks, leba bread, leba bread, and leba bread.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Whoa—!
Regulus pulls out the lamb as quickly as a flash and devours the meat.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah! Lamb! It tastes so good ... sooo gooood! I barely know what grease is supposed to taste like oooooooh ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: *chewing* ... Thank the great god of rock for his blessings! This Pirate finally gets some meat to eat!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Huh? It is me you should thank, the goddess of victory who soon brings you freedom.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Bring us freedom soon? May I ask ... how should I interpret your words?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Heh heh.
Lilya sits down on the ground.
She opens one of the cans and pours the drink into her mouth.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You want some?
Druvis takes the drink from her and takes a sip.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Thank you so much for coming alone and providing us with supplies, Lilya ...

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: However, please tell us why you are here.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: ... Did Madam Z send you?
Lilya shakes her head. She gives out four fingers.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Already been four and a half weeks. Right?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: This is not the first time I visit you guys here.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: The one hiding in the shadow last time ... It's you?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I wonder how much longer you can hold on for Vertin.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You see, saying is one thing, fighting is another.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I've seen many deserters. Way too many.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Crying out loud, peeing their pants, drooling all over on their rabbit foot ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But you guys are different.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You actually did it. You conquered places in the Foundation, defended your own places, and put pressure on those in white till this day, the last day in this four weeks and a half.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: That's the iron will I appreciate.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And if I didn't come today, would you eat your boots tomorrow?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Of course not. We still have potatoes. Almost ripe.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: And carrots!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Hahahahaha!

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Thank you for your kindness, Ms. Lilya. May I take it that you are coming to bring us the good news?

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Is there a final result for Madam Z's draft?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So far as I know, Madam Z hasn't given up yet.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Just like you, when she gets serious, she looks like a fierce doe.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: But I already lost my patience.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Tons of "processes" need to be done before it can be performed, even if the draft is passed at the final vote.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: As long as Vertin is still on that bed in the ward, you are just an isolated island.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Everyone can step on you.
Lilya stands up and pats off the dust on her carelessly.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: "Take care of them for me when necessary."

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: That's what Vertin said when she gave me the vodka.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It's time to deliver on my promise.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Are you going to do something dangerous?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A thing that is worth the risk.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I've been waiting for this moment for so long.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Someone needs to wake up from the dream.
TO BE CONTINUED…
